paragraphs.text: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is an autosomal recessive disease. It appears within the first weeks of life and is marked by a selective failure to absorb dietary glucose and galactose from the intestine. The resulting severe diarrhea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are removed from the diet (Turk et al., 1991). The disorder is caused by a defect in the intestinal brush border Na+/glucose cotransporter SGLT1 (Martín et al., 1996).

checks.evidence_quote: The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet.

paragraphs.text: Elsas et al. (1970) studied a 3-year-old girl with congenital glucose-galactose malabsorption and her family. In vitro, her jejunal mucosa was unable to concentrate glucose throughout a 60-minute incubation period. She also had a partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption. Both of her parents and a half sister showed impaired intestinal glucose transport. Her asymptomatic brother had normal transport.

paragraphs.text: Abdullah et al. (1996) reported 8 Arab children with glucose-galactose malabsorption from 8 different families. Six were Saudi Arabs and 2 were of other Arab nationalities. They were first seen for chronic watery diarrhea, present since birth, and failure to thrive. The mean age at presentation was 10.6 months. One child had a renal stone at the first visit, and another was found to have one on follow-up.

paragraphs.text: Elsas et al. (1970) found that jejunal mucosa from both parents of an affected girl (obligate heterozygotes) and from her half sister had glucose transport values between normal and those of the proband. Influx was impaired but efflux was normal. Kinetic analysis showed a reduced Vmax with a normal Km for glucose transport. Fructose accumulation was similar in all subjects. Renal glucose titration showed that the proband's absent intestinal glucose transport was accompanied by a partial impairment of renal glucose reabsorption. Her unaffected brother had a normal titration curve.
